payload.title: Interactive Wedding Seating Charts We Love
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their 30s, about 6 to 12 months from a destination or luxury wedding of 60 to 150 guests, who has (or is about to have) a guest list and table plan and now wants a seating display that guests actually enjoy, while making sure it still works on the night: readable, quick to use at the entrance, accessible, weatherproof and easy to change at the last minute.
payload.goal: Open Wonderland Studio and start the table plan (Try Wonderland Studio).
payload.angle: Most interactive seating chart roundups are photo galleries. This one sorts the ideas by what the guest actually does at the display (takes something, finds something, or does something) and pairs every idea with the practical check that decides whether it works on the night: how it reads, how it is ordered, where it sits and how people flow past it, who it leaves out, what weather does to it, and what happens when a guest changes at the last minute. It starts from the point page-one galleries skip: the display is only as good as the table plan behind it, so build the plan first, then choose the style. For destination weddings it adds the venue questions (setup space, outdoor rules, power, who sets up and packs down) that decide which styles are even possible.
must_include: INTRO-DEFINITION: in the first 100 words, a plain two to three sentence definition of an interactive seating chart (a seating display where each guest takes, finds or does something to learn their table, instead of only reading a board), plus who it suits.

PLAN-FIRST + HEAD LINK: early (within the first two sections, before the ideas) and prominent: finish the table plan before choosing a display style. Link the head guide /expert-advice/wedding-seating-chart here as the how-to for building the plan, and link /wonderland-studio as the place to build it (Wonderland Studio is our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs). Describe Studio only as 'planning app (seating chart, RSVP)'; any other feature claim is [[VERIFY]].

IDEAS GROUP 1, GUESTS TAKE SOMETHING: escort cards (including cards that double as table decor), name tags tied to a sweet treat or favour, a welcome drink with the name and table attached (champagne, or a coconut or chilled drink for a tropical setting), keys on a board or hooks. Keep these old-page ideas, rewritten from scratch: sweet treat, escort card as decor, glass of champagne, colourful take-home favour, tropical drink.

IDEAS GROUP 2, GUESTS FIND SOMETHING: a seating wall (photos or cards pinned to a wall or frame), a map-style chart (tables named after places that matter to the couple or the destination), a mirror or glass panel with names written on it, personal photos with a short message attached to the table number (kept from the old page).

IDEAS GROUP 3, GUESTS DO SOMETHING: a digital screen or QR-style lookup that guests use on arrival, and a display that doubles as a photo moment (kept from the old 'art of technology' idea, described generically). No product or app names.

PRACTICAL DETAILS SECTION: readability (letter size, contrast, lighting at night), order by surname or by table and when each is better, placement and flow at the entrance (several access points, distance from the bar or doors, not at a bottleneck), accessibility (seated-height reading, large print, a helper or host for guests who need it, not relying on a phone alone), outdoor weather (wind, sun glare, rain, heat on edible or floral elements, a covered backup), late changes (how each style handles a swap, who holds the master list on the day).

DESTINATION WEDDINGS: a short checklist of questions to ask the venue: where the display can stand and when it can be set up, outdoor and wind or rain rules, power for screens, whether items can be fixed to walls, who sets up and packs down, delivery of printed or fragile pieces, and language for international guests. Details a venue does not publish are written 'not published' and go on the booking checklist.

FAQ: 4 to 6 short questions, e.g. what is an interactive seating chart; do we still need a table plan; alphabetical or by table; how far ahead to finalise names; what if it rains; how to handle guests who change last minute.

CLOSE: one line pointing to a Wedded Advisor, worded from brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30 only (e.g. one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, with someone on the ground looking after the days that matter). Secondary CTA /wonderland-concierge. No hard sell.
avoid: Any vendor, stationer, photographer, Instagram account or third-party app name (including old-page credits).
Prices, costs, statistics, survey figures or 'trend' claims (old page said seating charts would 'take off in 2024': drop).
'Best', superlatives, rankings, and research talk ('studies show', 'we analysed', 'according to data').
Reusing any wording or images from the old page or from competitors; old images are reference only.
Clichés from the persona turn-offs (fairytale, dream day).
Restating the full how-to-build-a-seating-chart method: that belongs to /expert-advice/wedding-seating-chart; summarise and link.
Etiquette debate on whether to have a seating chart at all: owned by /expert-advice/wedding-without-seating-chart; link once if relevant.
American spelling (favor, color, organize) and em dashes.
Colons or dashes in the title; the title is fixed.
payload.cannibalisation_check: No other page targets 'interactive seating chart wedding'. Related: /expert-advice/wedding-seating-chart (head, owns the how-to: this post links to it early and does not repeat the method); /expert-advice/how-to-make-a-wedding-seating-chart (how-to, possibly overlapping the head; not this post's intent); /expert-advice/11-interactive-wedding-ideas-your-guests-will-love (interactive ideas across the whole day; this post is limited to the seating display, cross-link once); /expert-advice/wedding-without-seating-chart (draft, owns open seating); /expert-advice/prismm-vs-wonderland-studio (app comparison, not linked as it names a third-party app). This page itself ranks avg position 3.9 (1,271 impressions), so the refresh keeps its intent and URL.
